body:
TK proposes to spend 458 pages on chaff, rather than wheat.

As for his view of morality and murder,
 TK did not have high ideals -- as a young person, he once tried to justify his
bad
thoughts toward other people.
Then, one day while walking past
a girl he didn't like, he thought
to himself, "hey, I can hate anyone
I like and be free of this silly morality 
business."  (Someone would have
to remind me of the exact words).

TK is not bound up or 
guided by a higher morality -- he 
just long ago resolved to be free to
act on his hatred (like the time he waited
for Ellen B. with a knife because she
didn't want to go on a second date
with him).

__________

"[H]e fails to establish WHY some of the things he regards as "good" or "evil"
for man ARE so, and so, doesn't really establish a framework of morality within
which he may make some of the assertions about man's needs which he makes. 
Furthermore, I found that his reasoning tends to get a bit shaky when he moves
on to the more crucial issues, viz., why his particular advocacy of violent
attack against INDIVIDUAL scientists and businessmen is justifiable, given that
it is LARGE organizations and the technology that they support which are "to
blame" in his Weltanschauung.
		Robert S Kissel	
		in alt.fan.unabomber"	

"Beware when the great God lets loose a thinker on this planet.  Then all
things are at risk...  The very hope of man, the thoughts of his heart, the
religion of nations, the manners and morals of mankind are all at the mercy of
a new generalization."
		Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series (1841)

  "In modern society, achieving the strength, wisdom, and reverence of the epic
